metadata.title: Signal Propagation Properties in the Drosophila melanogaster Connectome: Intermodal Isolation, Differential Motor Access, and Non-Trivial Temporal Amplification
metadata.description:
Version 2.0. Supersedes v1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19136948), which remains available and is not withdrawn. This version applies the corrections listed in the accompanying erratum (file Mendieta2026_Paper1_Erratum_v1.0.pdf). The most consequential is a 32-bit integer overflow that inflated graph density 9.42-fold in v1.0: the density analysis of motor access is recomputed (three classes enriched, four depleted, one within expectation, against zero enriched in v1.0), and the reciprocity over-representation factor of 36x is withdrawn and replaced by ranks against null ensembles. The remaining corrections concern counts, the number of compatible neural models, the temporal parameter, data availability, licences and references. Version 2.0 adds a multi-hop analysis of motor access against a neuropil-preserving null, which shows that the modality ordering reflects neuropil co-location and that direct sensory-to-motor contacts are restricted within the shared neuropil.

Using the complete FlyWire v783 connectome (138,639 neurons; 15,091,983 directed connections carrying 54,492,922 synapses), three compatible parameter-free neural models and four null-model families, the paper characterizes three signal propagation properties of the Drosophila melanogaster brain: active intermodal isolation (contralateral cancellation 1.37; post-stimulus amplification requires specific wiring, Z_CP = +14.8 sigma), differential motor access set by anatomy and restricted within it (gustatory afferents contact 10 brain motor neurons where co-location predicts 101.6, z = -78.9), and non-trivial temporal amplification (cosine RDI from 0.63 to 0.83 post-stimulus under SparseLTC dynamics; reproduced by the linear model, not by LIF-soft). Reciprocity (26.60%; 13.98% under the five-synapse threshold) exceeds a degree- and block-preserving null 20.59-fold and is reported resolved over directed pairs of functional cell classes.

Code, raw logs and the manuscript source: https://github.com/gatehot59-star/drosophila-fep-connectome
metadata.notes: Version 2.0 of the preprint deposited on 20 March 2026 (v1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.19136948). The erratum file lists every correction against v1.0. Not peer reviewed.
